cases.title: Amazon–Anthropic: funded vendor equity and a compute-delivery-linked financing facility

dossier.title: Amazon–Anthropic: funded vendor equity and a compute-delivery-linked financing facility

entities.name: Anthropic outside investors and customers
roles: potential external capital and customer-cash ingress; distinct populations

first_public_clocks.event: Named partnership and up-to-USD4bn minority investment announced
>USD100bn / 10-year AWS commitment; USD5bn current and up to USD20bn future capital announced
Series H announcement includes USD5bn Amazon participation
Quarter-end funded amounts and detailed delivery-linked facility disclosed in 10-Q accepted July 30 18:11:13; filing date July 31

dossier.assessment: Strongly documented vendor-capital / purchase relationship; real deployment evidence; independence of ultimate customer cash coverage remains unmeasured. No finding of fabricated revenue.

sections.Structure and first public clocks: Amazon invests in the same firm that purchases AWS capacity and distributes Claude through Amazon Bedrock. The September 25, 2023 announcement established the named relationship: up to USD4bn of minority capital, AWS as primary cloud, and collaboration on Trainium/Inferentia. This creates two economic benefits for Amazon—investment returns and cloud/chip demand—without proving that any particular investment dollar later became AWS revenue. Keep that first public clock separate from the much larger April 20, 2026 expansion and the later SEC disclosure of its financing mechanics. [AI_A01] [AI_A02] [AI_A05]
sections.Financing, execution and equity rights: Amazon's June 2026 filing identifies USD8bn invested in convertible notes during Q3 2023–Q4 2025, followed by USD5bn Series G and USD5bn Series H preferred-stock investments in Q2 2026. Cumulative funded capital is therefore USD18bn, a calculation rather than a separate issuer headline. The new facility began with a USD20bn cap; Series H participation reduced the remaining cap to USD15bn. Availability depends on AWS delivery milestones, with Anthropic choosing draws. Funding purchases notes or, after a liquidity event, common stock subject to an ownership cap. The facility expires 30 months after an Anthropic liquidity event. Nonvoting equity and convertibles do not establish a control acquisition. [AI_A03]
sections.Commercial obligation and performance: Anthropic announced a commitment exceeding USD100bn over ten years for AWS technology, alongside capacity of up to 5GW. The announcement covers Trainium 2–4 and Graviton and includes future-silicon options; it should not be read as a fixed quantity of already delivered chips. Amazon's filing confirms contractual chip-performance obligations. The full schedule of enforceable minimum spend, rebates, cancellation damages, service credits, assignment rights, prepayment requirements and termination conditions is unavailable in inspected sources. This is a documented purchase commitment with performance conditions, not evidence that every announced dollar is unconditional or already recognized. [AI_A02] [AI_A03]
sections.Revenue, cash, delivery and utilization: In April, Anthropic reported using over one million Trainium2 chips to train and serve Claude; almost 1GW of additional Trainium2/3 capacity was expected during 2026. The first statement is operational evidence supplied by the customer; the second is forward capacity. Neither supplies utilization percentages. The same announcement reports over 100,000 Bedrock customers. Those customers can include free, trial or mixed-volume accounts, so account counts do not measure independent cash. Anthropic-specific AWS revenue, cash collections, receivables and deferred revenue are not separately reported in inspected filings. Amazon's investment remeasurement gains belong to investment accounting, not cloud sales or cash receipts. [AI_A02] [AI_A03]
sections.External capital, end customers and publ: Anthropic's May 28 Series H announcement reports USD65bn raised, including USD15bn of previously committed hyperscaler money. Amazon's USD5bn is inside that total. Named financial investors show that financing extends beyond AWS; named semiconductor investors also benefit from infrastructure growth, so the remainder cannot all be labeled economically disinterested capital. Anthropic also reports a USD47bn revenue run rate reached earlier in May. That is a current-rate extrapolation, not audited annual revenue or cash collection. No case-specific government grant, guarantee, procurement cash, warrant or subsidy amount was established in these sources. Absence of a disclosed amount is not proof that no public support exists. [AI_A04]
sections.Dependencies and economically benign exp: The capital facility explicitly connects AWS delivery with financing availability. A delivery miss could slow both compute expansion and access to vendor capital, while sustained customer demand could require still more capacity. This is an execution dependency, not a demonstrated insolvency trigger. The benign explanation has economic support: co-development of specialized chips and an established distribution channel can reduce unit costs and speed customer access; existing training/serving deployments indicate productive equipment use. Multiple other capital providers weaken a claim that Anthropic is wholly captive to one financier. However, vendor variety does not establish immediate workload portability or prove profitable unit economics. [AI_A01] [AI_A02] [AI_A04]
sections.Falsifiers, unknowns and metric limits: A fragility thesis would weaken with audited third-party customer cash, durable positive contribution margins after full inference costs, capacity delivered on schedule, and ordinary financing raised without tied purchases. It would strengthen with persistent usage shortfalls, repeated vendor-funded renewals, large disputed receivables, or released contractual terms showing obligations that substantially exceed independent cash generation. Those are tests, not findings. Do not divide USD18bn funded equity by USD100bn of ten-year purchase commitments and call the quotient a financed-demand share: different periods, cash-flow categories and overlapping financing rounds defeat that denominator. Present funded cash, conditional capital, purchase commitments and utilization as separate observations.

Exact enforceable minimums, cancellation damages and chip-performance remedies
Actual drawn amount of remaining USD15bn facility after June 30

dossier.assessment: Capital/supply overlap established, but exact named cash funding is not recovered from opened primary records. Supplier diversity is documented; current financial independence is not.

sections.Structure and public clocks: Google is both a capital provider and a seller/distributor of services used by Anthropic. The public cloud partnership began February 3, 2023. A later CMA decision describes an October 2022 side letter, but that historic contract date must not be used as the date the public could know its terms. The November 19, 2024 decision's full text became public December 24. It identifies nonvoting equity, convertible debt, a nonexclusive compute commitment, and nonexclusive Vertex AI distribution. The distinction matters for event studies: a previously confidential term can only enter a public information set when disclosed. [AI_G01] [AI_G02]
sections.Capital, rights and disclosure limits: The CMA redacts dollar amounts and parts of the supply timetable. It records no board representation rights, conversion into nonvoting shares, and no commercial-policy veto establishing material influence under the test applied. These are useful governance facts, not a finding that Anthropic's financing or demand is economically independent. Exact cash funded, current ownership, note maturities and any later revised governance terms remain unknown here. Alphabet's June 2026 filing includes an anonymous private-company future capital commitment of USD20bn, contingent on milestones through 2030. It does not name Anthropic; that amount is excluded from this case's named capital totals. [AI_G02] [AI_G06] [AI_G07]
sections.Commercial commitments and capacity: On October 23, 2025, Anthropic announced an expansion involving up to one million Google TPUs, valued imprecisely at tens of billions of dollars, with well over 1GW expected online during 2026. On April 6, 2026, it announced multiple gigawatts of additional next-generation TPU capacity expected to come online starting in 2027. Broadcom's same-day 8-K names approximately 3.5GW through Broadcom as part of the broader commitment. Anthropic's May Series H release later describes the Google–Broadcom arrangement as 5GW. The 3.5GW component and 5GW envelope must not be added to produce 8.5GW. [AI_G03] [AI_G04] [AI_G05] [AI_A04]
sections.Conditions, recognized economics and rea: Broadcom says consumption depends on Anthropic's continuing commercial success and that it is working with operational and financial partners. That is a meaningful risk qualification, but the public wording does not reveal an enforceable customer cancellation right. The full capacity contract, minimum cash payments, acceptance tests, service credits, equity incentives, termination rights and default waterfall were not obtained. Google-specific Anthropic revenue, customer collections, receivables and deferred balances are not quantified. TPU use is established qualitatively; utilization of the announced future gigawatts is not. A capacity reservation should remain a commitment edge until delivery and consumption are separately evidenced. [AI_G03] [AI_G05]
sections.Outside demand, alternatives and public: Anthropic repeatedly describes a three-platform strategy spanning Google TPUs, AWS Trainium and Nvidia GPUs, while naming AWS its primary cloud/training partner. The CMA reviewed multiple financing sources and sales channels and found insufficient evidence of Google material influence at that time. This gives the benign alternative more support than a bare claim that a successful startup can refinance indefinitely. Anthropic's customer-growth and revenue-run-rate disclosures provide demand indicators, but they are affiliated statements and do not isolate independent cash collected or gross margins on Google compute. No case-specific government grant, procurement, public guarantee or tax-credit amount was established. [AI_G02] [AI_G03] [AI_G04]
sections.Dependency analysis and competing benign: A supplier investing in a major customer can share development risk, secure demand for specialized silicon, and help a customer optimize workloads. Multi-vendor procurement can improve bargaining power and reduce exposure to a single technology roadmap. These are plausible productive reasons for the relationship, supported by named deployments across alternative platforms. The remaining fragility hypothesis concerns economics and timing: customer revenue might fail to grow fast enough to absorb reserved capacity, or migration and chip qualification could take longer than financing assumptions allow. Nonexclusive contracts permit alternatives but do not make alternative capacity instantly available. No cash round trip or fictitious revenue is established.
sections.Falsifiers and exclusions: The strongest falsifiers would be audited independent customer cash sufficient to service compute costs, verified broad TPU utilization, transparent cancellation/acceptance terms, and outside financing without commercial ties. Evidence of repeated vendor-supported extensions, unused reserved capacity, or obligations concentrated in one platform would instead strengthen dependency concerns. Do not import a media-reported USD40bn Google investment or USD200bn Google purchase headline into primary-verified totals without named primary documents. Likewise, Broadcom's later anonymous XPV financing, guarantee and convertible-note facility are excluded from the named Anthropic graph; a shared sector, technology or timing is insufficient counterparty identification. The appendix preserves that relevant evidence without manufacturing a link. [AI_B01]

dossier.assessment: Actual financial-market capital and actual compute use coexist with very large overlapping commitments. The public record does not allocate Oracle-wide balances to OpenAI or convert Stargate's program envelope into funded cash.

sections.Program, entities and initial promise: Stargate's January 21, 2025 announcement describes a new company intending to invest USD500bn over four years and begin deploying USD100bn immediately. It names SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX as initial equity funders, with SoftBank responsible for finance and OpenAI for operations. It also says definitive agreements were still being finalized. The headline therefore belongs to an announced program envelope, not a verified USD500bn financing close. Microsoft, Nvidia and Arm's technical participation does not itself establish equal equity funding. A White House launch is not proof of a federal guarantee, grant or procurement payment. [AI_S01]
sections.Purchase commitments and overlapping cap: OpenAI's September 23, 2025 update expressly states that its Oracle partnership exceeds USD300bn over five years. That is named primary evidence for the headline, although the complete enforceable contract is unavailable. The same page connects nearly 7GW of planned capacity with more than USD400bn of investment and identifies up to 4.5GW of additional Oracle capacity. These overlap the original Stargate program and must not be summed. The page reports first GB200 racks at Abilene in June and early training/inference. A later October site update should be distinguished from the September information clock. [AI_S02]
sections.Actual capital and equity: SoftBank's March 31, 2025 investment agreement, announced April 1, initially contemplated up to USD40bn with USD10bn syndicated and staged closing conditions linked to OpenAI's restructuring. Its convertible instruments included preferred/common conversion provisions. That historic conditional envelope is superseded for cash-status purposes by later executed disclosures. On October 1, 2026, SoftBank reported completing the third USD10bn tranche of its 2026 USD30bn follow-on investment. It put cumulative OpenAI investment at USD64.6bn and ownership near 13%. These are equity injections into OpenAI, not demonstrated spending on a particular Stargate campus. [AI_S04] [AI_S07]
sections.Debt, maturity and correction of the cur: SoftBank executed a USD40bn unsecured bridge facility in March 2026, originally maturing March 25, 2027, with major banks as lenders. A facility limit does not prove that the full amount was drawn. September issuance terms cover USD10bn and EUR1bn of senior notes, with USD coupons of 8.625%, 9.250% and 9.750% and maturities in 2030, 2032 and 2034. The October release traces the final OpenAI tranche to those notes. It also states that all March bridge borrowings were repaid and the final undrawn capacity canceled. An unresolved March 2027 maturity crisis is therefore contrary to the latest evidence. Coupons alone do not identify a subsidy or credit spread. [AI_S05] [AI_S06] [AI_S07]
sections.Oracle revenue, prepayments and external: Oracle's August 31, 2026 filing reports USD664bn of remaining performance obligations, USD11.4bn of quarterly customer prepayments with a significant financing component, and USD19.9bn net proceeds from its completed share-sale program. The prepayments are cash received before corresponding services; they are not all recognized revenue. The equity issuance shows outside financial capital reaching the infrastructure supplier. All three amounts are company-wide and the filing does not name OpenAI as their sole source or beneficiary. OpenAI-specific receivables, deferred balances, collections, cancellation terms and guaranteed minimum payments remain unknown. Do not allocate anonymous balances by assuming the largest reported customer generated everything. [AI_S08]
sections.Delivered capacity, dependencies and ben: By April 29, 2026, OpenAI said it had secured more than 10GW and that GPT-5.5 had been trained at Abilene on OCI and Nvidia GB200 systems. The training claim is concrete sponsor-reported use; secured gigawatts are a broader commitment measure. No site-wide utilization percentage follows from either. The benign explanation is that shared development, outside equity and term debt can fund long-lived infrastructure while workloads and revenue grow. Physical training activity supports that explanation. Power, permitting, transmission, construction and partner readiness remain dependencies that can delay revenue conversion even where capital is already committed. [AI_S03]
sections.Falsifiers, government layer and denomin: No comprehensive public-financing, procurement or guarantee amount for the whole program is established in these sources. Keep any separately documented Nvidia/SB Energy guarantees in their own case and flag project overlaps. A fragility thesis would weaken with verifiable delivery milestones, capacity utilization, diversified paying customers, matched asset financing and customer cash sufficient for contractual payments. It would strengthen with stalled sites, customer prepayments masking weak recurring collections, or financing dependent on repeatedly extending supplier support. External bank/bond/equity financing is real ingress, but it still expects repayment or returns; it is not final customer demand. No valid network cash-ingress ratio can be calculated from these overlapping program, company and customer totals.

dossier.title: Talen–Amazon Susquehanna: paid asset purchase, long-term power demand and conditional nuclear support

first_public_clocks.event: Campus sale executed March 1; initial seller announcement March 4; named buyer/price explicit in opened March 14 follow-up
FERC rejects specific amended 300-to-480MW interconnection agreement
Expanded AWS PPA through 2042, up to 1920MW, approximately USD18bn notional revenue
Revised front-of-meter PPA transition occurs April 2026; confirmed in June-quarter filing, exact filing clock not recovered

dossier.assessment: Useful weak-circularity control: a paid asset sale and power contract with an operating customer, without disclosed reverse capital from Talen to Amazon. Regulatory and capped-demand risks remain; nuclear support is price contingent.

sections.Asset purchase and cash execution: Talen sold the campus to AWS on March 1, 2024 and announced the sale March 4. Its March 14 results explicitly identify the buyer and USD650m gross price. The later annual filing records USD350m at closing and USD300m released from escrow in August 2024. Proceeds financed debt repayment and other transaction distributions; a reported sale gain is not electricity revenue. The original arrangement contemplated up to 960MW, ramped in 120MW increments, with an Amazon option to cap at 480MW. This is an executed asset sale plus a demand contract, not disclosed Talen equity funding of Amazon's purchases. [AI_T01] [AI_T02] [AI_T03]
sections.Expanded contract and future value: On June 11, 2025, Talen announced an expanded PPA through 2042 for up to 1,920MW, with full volumes expected by 2032 and extension options. Its presentation describes approximately USD18bn of notional revenue over seventeen years. That is an estimate of future contractual sales, not cash received, recognized revenue or the value of a financial guarantee. The amendments remove Amazon's earlier 480MW cap option. The visual schedule shows full-quantity minimum and maximum levels of 1,680MW and 1,920MW by 2032. Other years' ramp values should be read from the actual schedule rather than interpolated into hard promises. [AI_T05] [AI_T06] [AI_T07]
sections.Minimums, shortfall protection and limit: The presentation describes a capped shortfall make-whole and estimates that, if no power were drawn, it could cover 50–65% of the full illustrative impact depending on market prices. The chart's denominator is incremental Amazon-PPA adjusted free cash flow beyond the prior co-location arrangement. It is not a promise to pay 50–65% of all USD18bn gross revenue. This is partial contractual demand protection, with market-price dependence and a cap. The full agreement, exact pricing formula, termination triggers, credit collateral and payment waterfall were not obtained. Record the minimum/offtake economics without upgrading the arrangement to an unlimited take-or-pay guarantee. [AI_T06] [AI_T07]
sections.Regulatory setback and completed transit: FERC's November 1, 2024 order rejected the specific amended interconnection agreement increasing co-located load from 300MW to 480MW. It was not a ban on all nuclear-powered data centers. The 2025 amendment instead described a transition to front-of-meter delivery: Susquehanna supplies PJM, Talen's retail provider supplies the customer, and PPL delivers transmission service. The June 2026 filing confirms that the transition occurred in April 2026. This is realized execution progress following a regulatory setback. It does not prove that the entire future 1,920MW is now delivered or that data center utilization is at its final design level. [AI_T04] [AI_T05] [AI_T08]
sections.Recognized economics and selective publi: Talen's 2025 annual accounts report USD220m of nuclear production tax-credit revenue in 2024 and none in 2025, explaining that 2025 prices exceeded the applicable threshold. Recognition is not necessarily contemporaneous cash collection. The IRS describes Section 45U as output-based support that declines with gross receipts, with prevailing-wage conditions affecting its rate. This is a concrete example of conditional revenue support coexisting with private power contracting; it does not establish perpetual subsidy or full government protection for the AWS PPA. Amazon-specific power revenue, receivables, deferred revenue and collections are not separately quantified in the opened records. [AI_T03] [AI_T09]
sections.Independent cash and competing benign ex: The observed USD650m asset consideration is actual customer cash reaching Talen, but AWS is an intermediate infrastructure buyer, so it should not be relabeled ultimate AI end-customer receipts. No reverse Talen investment, vendor loan or warrant funding Amazon was disclosed in this evidence set. Economically, an existing nuclear generator can exchange volatile merchant exposure for contracted power demand, while a data center secures a predictable supply. The front-of-meter structure preserves a connection to the broader electricity market, offering an alternative use for generation if a particular AI load underperforms. That mitigation has substance, although replacement market prices could be lower. [AI_T02] [AI_T05]
sections.Dependencies, falsifiers and disciplined: The remaining risks include nuclear availability, grid delivery, customer load ramp, market prices affecting shortfall economics, and counterparty payment performance. A fragility thesis would weaken with sustained delivered MWh, collected invoices, contract-compliant minimum payments and resilient cash flow under conservative merchant-price scenarios. It would strengthen with repeatedly delayed load, uncollected shortfall claims, outages or obligations that exceed recoverable value. Public support should be measured using credits actually earned and eventually collected, with qualification and clawback rules preserved. Do not add Amazon's separate Pennsylvania data center capital plan to the USD18bn PPA value. The strongest control result is a conventional paid asset/offtake relationship with partial risk sharing, not proof that all AI-linked power demand is durable.
